\ No newline at end of file
+# jobs-worker
+
+A prototype job worker service that provides an API to run arbitrary Linux processes
+
+# Design
+
+There are 3 primary components to the jobs-worker:  The `Library`, `Server`, and `CLI Client`.  Each is outlined in detail below
+
+## Library
+
+The Library component exposes an API to do the following:
+
+* Start a job which is capable of executing an arbitrary Linux process
+  * Resource control is optionally accessible to this API
+* Stop a running job
+* Obtain status about a job (running or completed/existed)
+* Stream the output of a job (running or completed/existed)
+
+A high level worker API is defined below.  
+
+```go
+type Worker interface {
+	StartJob(ctx context.Context, cmd Command) (*Job, error)
+	StopJob(ctx context.Context, jobID string) error
+	GetJobStatus(ctx context.Context, jobID string) (*JobStatus, error)
+	StreamJobOutput(ctx context.Context, jobID string) (<-chan string, error)
+}
+```
+
+For a more detailed and complete API [godoc](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/cmd/godoc) can be used.
+
+If you have docker installed on your machine you can run `make godoc` from a CLI.  
+This will build a self-contained image to generate the docs without the need to have godoc installed locally.  
+
+If you do not have docker installed you will need to install godoc yourself using the following command
+
+```
+go install golang.org/x/tools/cmd/godoc@latest
+```
+
+Once installed fire up the docs using the following command:
+
+```
+godoc -http=:8080
+```
+
+Regardless of the approach used, the docs will be accessible at [localhost:8080](http://localhost:8080).
+
+### Storage
+
+#### Job Data
+
+For this exercise job state data will be stored in memory.  This is obviously not optimal as the data will be lost once the process interacting with this library completes/exits. 
+In an ideal situation we would store this data in persistent storage (i.e. database).  This would allow for the data to be retrieved outside the lifecycle of the process which is using this library.
+
+#### Logs
+
+Similar to job data, we will be storing the log files containing job output in memory.  Again, this is not an optimal solution for the above reason.  However, it's even worse as some processes can produce
+a considerable amount of output.  In an ideal world we would be able to store the log files in an external source, for example, an object storage bucket (i.e. S3, CF R2, Azure Blob, etc...).  While there are cost 
+implications to this, it would allow for us to have access to the logs outside the process lifecycle.  All of these cloud providers have SDKs that allow us to access the logs in a secure way (i.e. presigned URLs).
+
+### Logging & Error Handling
+I plan on using [logrus](https://github.com/sirupsen/logrus) to gain access to structured logging.  A `JSONFormatter` and log level of `DEBUG` will be set by default via an `init()` function.  
+A better approach would be to make logging more configurable via an API.  However, for the purpose of time, I am going to skip this. Developer log statements are logged at the `DEBUG` level.
+
+All errors will be "bubbled up" to the client and sentinel errors will be used when appropriate
+
+### Context Cancellation & Propagation
+All APIs within this library will have the first argument as [context.Context](https://pkg.go.dev/context).  This is to allow for future proper cancellation support out of the gate (assuming clients configure it correctly).
+In the future, the context can be leveraged to support monitoring/observability and tracing via APM.
+
+### Resource Control

+# jobs-worker
+
+A prototype job worker service that provides an API to run arbitrary Linux processes
+
+# Design
+

+## Library
+
+The Library component exposes an API to do the following:
+

+  * Resource control is optionally accessible to this API
+* Stop a running job
+* Obtain status about a job (running or completed/existed)
+* Stream the output of a job (running or completed/existed)

+
+```go
+type Worker interface {

+	StreamJobOutput(ctx context.Context, jobID string) (<-chan string, error)
+}
+```
+
+For a more detailed and complete API [godoc](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/cmd/godoc) can be used.
+

+This will build a self-contained image to generate the docs without the need to have godoc installed locally.  
+
+If you do not have docker installed you will need to install godoc yourself using the following command
+
+```
+go install golang.org/x/tools/cmd/godoc@latest
+```
+
+Once installed fire up the docs using the following command:
+
+```
+godoc -http=:8080
+```
+
+Regardless of the approach used, the docs will be accessible at [localhost:8080](http://localhost:8080).
+
+### Storage
+
+#### Job Data
+
+For this exercise job state data will be stored in memory.  This is obviously not optimal as the data will be lost once the process interacting with this library completes/exits. 
+In an ideal situation we would store this data in persistent storage (i.e. database).  This would allow for the data to be retrieved outside the lifecycle of the process which is using this library.
+
+#### Logs
+
+Similar to job data, we will be storing the log files containing job output in memory.  Again, this is not an optimal solution for the above reason.  However, it's even worse as some processes can produce
+a considerable amount of output.  In an ideal world we would be able to store the log files in an external source, for example, an object storage bucket (i.e. S3, CF R2, Azure Blob, etc...).  While there are cost 
+implications to this, it would allow for us to have access to the logs outside the process lifecycle.  All of these cloud providers have SDKs that allow us to access the logs in a secure way (i.e. presigned URLs).
+
+### Logging & Error Handling
+I plan on using [logrus](https://github.com/sirupsen/logrus) to gain access to structured logging.  A `JSONFormatter` and log level of `DEBUG` will be set by default via an `init()` function.  
+A better approach would be to make logging more configurable via an API.  However, for the purpose of time, I am going to skip this. Developer log statements are logged at the `DEBUG` level.
+
+All errors will be "bubbled up" to the client and sentinel errors will be used when appropriate
+
+### Context Cancellation & Propagation
+All APIs within this library will have the first argument as [context.Context](https://pkg.go.dev/context).  This is to allow for future proper cancellation support out of the gate (assuming clients configure it correctly).
+In the future, the context can be leveraged to support monitoring/observability and tracing via APM.
+
+### Resource Control
+
+When a job is started a client can optionally provide the ability to configure the resources the job has access to on the host machine.  To achieve this, [Control Groups (cgroups) V2](https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/cgroup-v2.txt) is being utilized.  
+Below are the resources that can be provided.
+
+**Memory**
+
+Max - The maximum amount of memory (in bytes) the job/process can consume prior to OOM (hard limit)
+
+Min - The minimum amount of memory (in bytes) to be given to the job/process
+
+**CPU** 
+
+Weight - the CPU time/cycles for the process
+
+Max - The maximum bandwidth limit in a given period
+
+CPUs - The requested CPU(s) to be used by the process
+
+**IO**
+
+Max - BPS (bytes per second) and IOPs for IO operations across device(s).
+
+#### Considerations
+
+* For the purposes of this exercise (and time), I will assume the provided resource values align with the cgroup V2 syntax.  However, in a more production like API/SDK I would provide a cleaner abstraction that would better
+facilitate supplying values that are not coupled to the underlying implementation (i.e. cgroups V2).  Doing this makes it much easier to change things "under the hood" without breaking existing clients.
+Errors returned from the cgroup controller interfaces due to invalid syntax will be "bubbled up" to the clients.
+
+* In order for resource management via cgroup V2 it needs to be mounted on the filesystem via `mount -t cgroup2 none $MOUNT_POINT`. 
+For the purposes of this exercise I will assume that `cgroup2` is enabled and mounted at `/sys/fs/cgroup/`.
+
+* In order for the library to work properly with cgroup V2, the execution environment must have `root` privileges. 
+For the purposes of this exercise I will assume that the execution environment where the server is running has `root` privileges.
+
+## Server
+The server will leverage the worker library to manage jobs.  The service will communicate to clients via [gRPC](https://grpc.io/).
+
+### IDL
+The gRPC server will be defined using the [Protobuf](https://protobuf.dev/) IDL found in the file `proto/worker.proto`.  
+The Protobuf compiler, `protoc`, will be used build the IDL.  The plugins `protoc-gen-go` and `protoc-gen-go-grpc` are required to properly build the necessary generated code.
+
+If you wish to build the generated code you can execute the command `make build-proto`.  This will create a docker image capable of compiling the code and placing it in the desired directory.
+This approach makes it so `protoc` and the plugins mentioned above are not needed on the machine of clients.  However, docker is required.
+
+## Client / CLI
+The client is a command line interface that will leverage the generated gRPC client code to communicate with the server.
+I plan on using [spf13/cobra](https://github.com/spf13/cobra) to assist in the creation of the CLI.
+
+## Authentication
+mTLS, via TLS 1.3, will be used for authentication between client and server.
+
+[OpenSSL](https://www.openssl.org/) will be used to generate CA (X.509), client, and server certificates.  
+RSA 4096 bit encryption will be used. 
+
+All certs will be stored in a `certs` directory at the root of this repository.  Obviously this is not a secure way of doing this as they will be visible in plain text within this repository.
+In a production environment I would consider leveraging an external key management service such as AWS KMS or HashiCorp Vault.  These certificate contents can then be injected
+into the services at runtime or fetched.
+
+## Authorization
+For an authorization scheme we will leverage `grpc.CallOption`s for client requests and `grpc.UnaryServerInterceptor` and `grpc.StreamServerInterceptor` on the server side.
+More specifically, a `grpc.PerRPCCredentials` call option will be populated with a token containing information about the user making the request.
+
+For simplicity, a hard coded, never expiring, plain text, "token" shared between client and server will be used.  The token will in the form of `user-email::role`.  The server will contain a hardcoded mapping of 
+user-email values and roles.  For requests with valid user-email and roles calls will succeed.  Invalid user-email/role pairs will fail.
+
+Again, this is obviously an insecure way of performing authorization given the plain text, hard coded, and long-lived nature of this approach.
comment.body: This scheme does not provide secure authz. You will need to describe a secure authorization system that does not re-implement the authentication provided by mTLS to meet the challenge requirements.

+	StreamJobOutput(ctx context.Context, jobID string) (<-chan string, error)
+}
+```
+
+For a more detailed and complete API [godoc](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/cmd/godoc) can be used.
+
+If you have docker installed on your machine you can run `make godoc` from a CLI.  
+This will build a self-contained image to generate the docs without the need to have godoc installed locally.  
+
+If you do not have docker installed you will need to install godoc yourself using the following command
+
+```
+go install golang.org/x/tools/cmd/godoc@latest
+```
+
+Once installed fire up the docs using the following command:
+
+```
+godoc -http=:8080
+```
+
+Regardless of the approach used, the docs will be accessible at [localhost:8080](http://localhost:8080).
+
+### Storage
+
+#### Job Data
+
+For this exercise job state data will be stored in memory.  This is obviously not optimal as the data will be lost once the process interacting with this library completes/exits. 
+In an ideal situation we would store this data in persistent storage (i.e. database).  This would allow for the data to be retrieved outside the lifecycle of the process which is using this library.
+
+#### Logs
+
+Similar to job data, we will be storing the log files containing job output in memory.  Again, this is not an optimal solution for the above reason.  However, it's even worse as some processes can produce
+a considerable amount of output.  In an ideal world we would be able to store the log files in an external source, for example, an object storage bucket (i.e. S3, CF R2, Azure Blob, etc...).  While there are cost 
+implications to this, it would allow for us to have access to the logs outside the process lifecycle.  All of these cloud providers have SDKs that allow us to access the logs in a secure way (i.e. presigned URLs).
+
+### Logging & Error Handling
+I plan on using [logrus](https://github.com/sirupsen/logrus) to gain access to structured logging.  A `JSONFormatter` and log level of `DEBUG` will be set by default via an `init()` function.  
+A better approach would be to make logging more configurable via an API.  However, for the purpose of time, I am going to skip this. Developer log statements are logged at the `DEBUG` level.
+
+All errors will be "bubbled up" to the client and sentinel errors will be used when appropriate
+
+### Context Cancellation & Propagation
+All APIs within this library will have the first argument as [context.Context](https://pkg.go.dev/context).  This is to allow for future proper cancellation support out of the gate (assuming clients configure it correctly).
+In the future, the context can be leveraged to support monitoring/observability and tracing via APM.
+
+### Resource Control
comment.body: I planned on creating a `cgroup` for each job, named with a `uuid` in the root cgroup directory mounted at `/sys/fs/cgroup`. Based on which parameters were provided, the appropriate controllers would be enabled in the `cgroup.subtree_control` file.  Once the job was created a new child cgroup would be created in the job directory using the PID of the job.  The PID would then be added to this directory.  Upon completion, the job and child cgroups would be cleaned up.

> What units / formats do these fields use?

For memory, all units are in `bytes`.  

For cpu weight is a value from 1-10000, max is defined in the format of `$MAX $PERIOD` where the period is defined in microseconds and max is the max bandwidth.  

For io, the following settings can be modified 

rbps | Max read bytes per second
-- | --
wbps | Max write bytes per second
riops | Max read IO operations per second
wiops | Max write IO operations per second

Regarding formatting of string inputs, as mentioned in the `Considerations` section of `Resource Control`, I plan on putting the onus of formatting on the clients for the sake of time.  Ideally, if time weren't an issue, I would implement something like k8s [resource.Quantity](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource#Quantity).  Is this acceptable?

comment.body:
> How do I create a worker? 

I am planning on exposing a constructor function, `New`, which would return an implementation of the `Worker` interface.  From a client perspective, it would read as follows: 

```go
package main

import (
	"github.com/lsiv568/jobs/lib/worker"
)

func main() {
    w := worker.New()
}
```

> What is this interface used for? 

The interface is used by clients to start and stop jobs, obtain their status, and query logs for jobs. 

> Why does the library need a centralized job manager with IDs?

While a centralized job manager with IDs is not absolutely necessary, I felt as though it would be a more developer friendly library.  As an alternative, if we want to leave state management up to the clients of the library, we do the following:

1. Have a `Start` API defined which will start a `Job` and return a `Job` struct / interface.
2. Expose `Stop`, `GetStatus`, and `StreamOutput` APIs on the `Job` struct / interface.  
 
What do you think of this approach?

**Note**
In my planned implementation I was going to keep these functions as private on the `Job` struct and leverage them from the `Worker` implementation.  This would result in management / job lookup in the `Worker` implementation and  encapsulate the functionality and logic within the `Job`.
